import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Vaught conjecture

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaught_conjecture)
-/

namespace VaughtConjecture

open FirstOrder.Language

/-- The number of countable models of some L-Theory T up to isomorphism -/
def numberOfCountableModels {L : FirstOrder.Language} (T : L.Theory) : Cardinal :=
  Cardinal.mk (Quotient (Setoid.comap
    (fun (model : {mt : T.ModelType // Countable mt.Carrier}) ↦
    CategoryTheory.Bundled.mk model.val.Carrier model.val.struc)
    equivSetoid))

/--
The Vaught conjecture states that for a countable language L and a complete L-Theory T
the number of countable models of T (up to isomorphism) is finite, $\aleph_0$ or $2^{\aleph_0}$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem vaught_conjecture {L : FirstOrder.Language} (hL : Countable L.Symbols)
                          {T : L.Theory} (hT : T.IsComplete) :
  numberOfCountableModels T ≤ Cardinal.aleph0 ∨ numberOfCountableModels T = Cardinal.continuum
  := by sorry

end VaughtConjecture

reformulations.difference: Wikipedia's detailed formulation assumes an infinite model and counts models of cardinality exactly ℵ₀. Lean allows every complete theory and counts finite as well as countably infinite models.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: If a complete theory has an infinite model, it has no finite models, so the two counts agree. Otherwise satisfiability, which is included in Mathlib's IsComplete, supplies a finite model. Every model of a complete theory with a finite model is isomorphic to that finite model, even in an infinite language: finitely many candidate bijections suffice to produce a distinguishing sentence if two finite models are not isomorphic. Thus the additional case has exactly one counted isomorphism class and automatically satisfies the first branch. Including this case does not strengthen the conjecture substantively.

reformulations.difference: The two occurrences of numberOfCountableModels elaborate with independent model-carrier universe levels, whereas the source uses a single model-counting cardinal.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every countable carrier is equivalent to a type in any universe. Transporting its first-order structure along such an equivalence preserves satisfaction and isomorphism. These transports induce mutually inverse maps on the quotients of countable models, so the counts agree after cardinal lifting. Aleph₀ and the continuum are preserved by lifting. The scratch file proves the quotient equivalence, equality of lifted counts, and mixed_universes_iff, showing that the elaborated disjunction is equivalent to one using the same model universe in both branches.

review.notes: Both declarations were checked. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles and independently verifies the quotient's isomorphism relation, universe invariance, the finite-or-ℵ₀ cardinal reformulation, zero count for unsatisfiable theories, and count one for both the singleton theory and the theory of an infinite pure set. The checks do not depend on sorryAx. Countability of all sentences and of T follows from Countable L.Symbols. The cited page still describes Knight's announced counterexample as unverified, so research open matches its recorded status. The linked Project Euclid article returned an access challenge; the cited Wikipedia page itself supplied an explicit statement and status.
